public.title: Tracks Without Footprints
public.incident: Fine ridges cross a coastal sand plot overnight, yet surface cameras show no animal walking the route.
public.atmosphere: The ridges weave beneath sparse vegetation and fade quickly after wind reaches the plot.
public.question: Which species left the pattern, and what process best explains the missing surface trail?

explanationChoices.label: Subsurface foraging
explanationChoices.description: A small digger is moving through shallow sand while hunting prey.

explanationChoices.label: Wind pattern
explanationChoices.description: Airflow around plants formed ridges that resemble animal tracks.

explanationChoices.label: Buried runoff
explanationChoices.description: Water beneath the surface displaced sand into narrow lines.

explanationChoices.label: A concealed large animal
explanationChoices.description: A larger visitor crossed the site outside the camera view.

explanationFeedback.subsurface-foraging: This mechanism fits a continuous ridge with no exposed walking trail.
explanationFeedback.wind-pattern: Wind erases the ridges, but their connected route beneath vegetation points to movement before erosion.
explanationFeedback.buried-runoff: The route branches around prey-rich vegetation rather than following slope or drainage.
explanationFeedback.large-animal: A large surface traveler should leave weight-bearing impressions as well as a visible camera passage.

resolution.headline: A hunter beneath the sand
resolution.diagnosis: De Winton’s golden mole made shallow subsurface runs while searching for small animal prey in soft coastal sand.
evidenceChain: The trace is a continuous ridge instead of separated footprints.
Movement stays within loose sand and beneath vegetation.
Diet evidence points to small invertebrate prey in the substrate.
resolution.ecologicalRole: Subsurface insectivores redistribute soil while consuming small prey, linking dune structure to its hidden food web.
resolution.taxonomy: Cryptochloris wintoni belongs to Chrysochloridae, the African golden mole family, not the true mole family Talpidae.
resolution.misconception: A surface ridge can record an animal that never walked on the surface.
rejectedAlternatives: Wind explains rapid disappearance, not the organized route.
Runoff would follow terrain rather than a foraging path beneath plants.
